transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (AtlasPay TPM), Carlos Ruiz (Infra Lead), Lara Chen (Director of ML), Ben Ortiz (Security)

Summary/Goals: Scoping POC to decide on hosted vs dedicated vs private. Gather success criteria, workload sizing, define benchmarks and timeline.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick introductions real quick?
[00:12] Priya (AtlasPay): Hi, this is Priya, TPM. we run payments product, building fraud detection & customer messaging. doing research into LLMs for dy- uh dynamic reply and risk scoring.
[00:24] Carlos (AtlasPay): Carlos here, infra lead, we'll need low latency for some paths, and want to understand networking/VPC implications.
[00:32] Lara (AtlasPay): Lara, ML lead, I'm focused on model quality, throughput, and ops around model rollouts.
[00:38] Ben (AtlasPay): Ben, security, wanting to verify encryption, KMS, audit logs, and compliance.
[00:44] Alex: Great, from Redwood we have Samir SE and me. goal today is to align on success criteria, get sizing, and propose a POC plan that lets you compare hosted/dedicated/private.

[01:05] Samir (Redwood SE): Quick agenda — 1) clarify workloads & traffic profiles, 2) success metrics (latency/throughput/cost/accuracy), 3) deployment constraints (data residency, SSO/KMS), 4) propose benchmark plan and timeline. sound ok?
[01:20] Priya: Yes. for context, we have two main workloads: a) user-facing chat replies — about 120 reqs/sec peak across region, p95 latency target 200ms, b) backend batch re-ranking for fraud signals, about 40 concurrent jobs, throughput-oriented.
[01:42] Lara: The chat prompts average 800 tokens input including system & few shots, outputs ~60 tokens. Re-ranking uses embeddings and a smaller sequence length.
[01:54] Carlos: Traffic is mostly NA with some EU. For some regulated customers we need EU data only for storage, though inferencing can be in NA if metadata is scrubbed, but we'd like options.

[02:10] Alex: Good specifics. can you confirm current infra? are you on AWS, do you have private subnets and a KMS?
[02:18] Carlos: AWS, EKS, we have private subnets and a customer-managed KMS in AWS. we can open peering, but prefer not to expose data to third-party storage.
[02:28] Ben: On compliance, we need SOC2 and logs, SSO via SAML, RBAC integration, and we'd like to see audit logs for queries.

[02:44] Samir: That's all supported across our modes but varies in effort: hosted -> easiest to start, Dedicated -> reserved capacity with VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS options, Private -> control plane in your VPC or on-prem but bigger lift. We'll map tradeoffs.

[03:10] Priya: Primary success criteria for the POC: 1) meet p95 latency for chat under realistic load, 2) cost target <$0.XX per 1k tokens (they were fuzzy), 3) model quality parity with our baseline (we'll provide eval prompts), 4) integration with KMS and audit logs.
[03:34] Lara: Add: ability to pin model versions and rollback during A/B.

[03:42] Alex: Great. on the cost target, can you give a ballpark of what you're comparing against?
[03:48] Priya: We're benchmarking against using an internal smaller model on CPU and also against OpenAI for quality/cost. our finance wants a predictable cost envelope.

[04:05] Samir: Noted. For sizing, a couple follow ups: can you share a 1-week trace with timestamps, request sizes, and percentiles? that'll let us estimate batching efficiency and kv-cache hit rates.
[04:18] Carlos: we can extract traces, but need guidance on fields we need to include.
[04:24] Samir: We'll send a small template. key fields: timestamp, input tokens, output tokens, region, endpoint type, and concurrency. anonymize user ids.
[04:40] Priya: We'll share top 50 prompts and 1 week of traces by next Friday.
[04:48] Alex: Great. now tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to get started — Redwood hosted API, stream responses, function calls, built-in quotas. pros are time-to-value and low ops. cons: multi-tenant and some customers worry about data residency/KMS.
[05:06] Samir: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — predictable latency and throughput, can bring your keys, VPC peering, and commit capacity. lower per-token cost at scale. cons: commit/contract, and longer lead time for capacity.
[05:25] Samir: Private is full VPC/on-prem; you run the control plane in your network and we provide the package. max isolation and compliance but highest integration effort and cost.
[05:40] Lara: If we hit 120 reqs/sec with 800 token inputs, what kind of latency we'd see on each mode? ballpark numbers are fine.
[05:50] Samir: Ballpark — Hosted with our optimized runtime using batching and prefix cache, we target p95=150-220ms for that size on our high-tier hosted instances but it depends on traffic burstiness. Dedicated with pinned capacity you can get p95 closer to 120-180ms and more consistent. Private depends on your infra but could match dedicated if you provision similar GPUs.
[06:14] Carlos: Does dedicated allow autoscaling during spikes?
[06:18] Alex: yes, dedicated supports autoscale policies and burst capacity, can be configured for your SLOs, but sustained spikes need committed capacity planning.
[06:30] Priya: For the re-ranking batch jobs, throughput matters and we'd prefer batching and quantized models to reduce cost — is that supported?
[06:38] Samir: Yes — we support quantized variants and can run batch re-ranking jobs on dedicated pools. dedicated and private let you choose inference configs and quantization to optimize cost. Hosted also has quantized model variants but availability depends on catalog.
[06:56] Ben: KMS — can we bring our own keys for encryption at rest and in transit? and are audit logs forwarded to our SIEM?
[07:05] Samir: For Dedicated you can BYOK (AWS KMS) and we support audit log forwarding to your syslog/S3. Hosted offers customer-managed keys for data at rest in many cases but with some limitations; we'll surface the exact docs. Private gives full control.
[07:26] Priya: Ok. timeline — we'd like to run a 4-week pilot. week 0 setup, week 1 baseline hosted run, week 2 dedicated sizing and baseline, week 3 benchmark runs and analysis, week 4 decision and next contract. Is that realistic?
[07:40] Alex: That's doable. We'll lay out a concrete timeline and responsibilities.
[07:48] Lara: Benchmarks — what metrics will Redwood collect? we'll need p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token cost, KV cache hit rate, and regression on our eval prompts.
[07:58] Samir: We'll capture all that plus GPU utilization and queueing latency. We'll provide a spreadsheet so you can compare host vs dedicated vs private.
[08:10] Carlos: For the dedicated option, what's the minimum commit?
[08:15] Alex: Depends on model and capacity; typical starters are X GPUs for a monthly commit — we'll send the dedicated sizing spreadsheet with examples. in many cases a small reserved pool is enough for initial pilot with burst capacity.
[08:32] Priya: How do we validate model parity? we need to ensure responses are not regressing.
[08:37] Lara: We'll run evals with the 50 prompts and accept A/B tests with canary rollouts.
[08:43] Alex: Redwood Optimize can run quality monitors and regression alerts tied to your prompt set. we'll set thresholds for acceptable deviation.
[08:56] Samir: A couple of technical details: KV cache behavior — if you have repeated prefixes (we often see in chat sessions), prefix/KV cache can reduce compute by 20-40% depending on hit rates. but sampling traces will let us estimate this.
[09:12] Priya: Good, we'll highlight repeated flows.
[09:18] Ben: On legal side, procurement and contract — what's typical for Dedicated vs Private? longer lead time for private?
[09:24] Alex: Yes, Dedicated usually has a commitment contract (monthly/annual) and some standard SLAs. Private involves enterprise licensing, infra agreements, and often a longer procurement cycle. we'll loop in legal once you decide to proceed.
[09:40] Carlos: Networking — VPC peering vs PrivateLink? which do you recommend?
[09:46] Samir: We support both. PrivateLink avoids cross-VPC routing changes and is generally simpler for tight security controls; VPC peering is fine if you control both sides. we'll diagram options in the follow-up.
[10:00] Priya: Let's talk success criteria thresholds: latency p95 <200ms for chat is must-have. cost per 1k tokens — finance wants a projected monthly spend within X% of current estimate. quality — no more than 5% degradation on our P0 prompts.
[10:20] Alex: We'll model those. For cost projections we need traffic traces and your current cost baseline.
[10:30] Samir: For benchmarks we propose: 1) Hosted baseline: run your prompt set against hosted API under replayed traffic for 24 hours, collect metrics. 2) Dedicated staging: provision a small dedicated pool, run same replay, measure and tune batching/quantization. 3) Optional Private dry-run if needed for compliance.
[10:58] Priya: For the hosted baseline can we stream responses and measure tail latency during bursts?
[11:05] Samir: yes, streaming is supported and we'll capture streamed vs non-streamed differences.
[11:14] Alex: Any blockers for starting the traces and pilot?
[11:18] Priya: We'll need the trace template and the security doc list. also an NDA is in place but procurement may need a SOW for dedicated.
[11:28] Alex: Ok we'll send the template and security doc checklist, and a sample SOW template for dedicated.
[11:36] Ben: One more on audit logs — do logs include full prompts or redacted? we need to ensure PII is not leaked.
[11:44] Samir: Logs can be configured to redact or hash inputs; for hosted we have redaction options, and for dedicated/private you control log retention and redaction. we'll include recommendations.
[11:58] Lara: Are there any known model regressions when switching quantized models? we care about quality for re-ranking especially.
[12:07] Samir: Quantization can impact some sensitive tasks; we'll include quality checks and recommend A/Bing on held-out evals before switching in prod. we can also suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[12:30] Alex: Next on timeline/touchpoints: 1) Alex sends pricing + dedicated sizing 2) Samir to prep benchmark harness & runbook 3) AtlasPay shares traces & prompts 4) schedule 2-hour kick off for the benchmark during week of 3/16.
[12:48] Priya: Sounds good. anything else on compliance?
[12:52] Ben: We'll review SOC2 and any contractual clauses, and may ask for an on-site review if private is pursued.
[13:00] Alex: Great. quick recap of tradeoffs: Hosted = fastest, least ops, some data residency limitations; Dedicated = predictable, BYOK, lower per-token cost at scale but contractual commit; Private = max control/compliance, highest lift.
[13:22] Carlos: For the pilot, maybe start with hosted baseline and a small dedicated pool in parallel — so we can compare.
[13:30] Lara: Agree, parallel runs will make the decision clearer within 4 weeks.
[13:38] Alex: We'll plan for parallel runs. Samir, we'll need your input on exact instance types to request for dedicated pool for 120 rps with 800 token in.
[13:48] Samir: I'll include example GPU profiles and expected throughput numbers in the spreadsheet. likely 4 A100-equivalent for the baseline, but we'll compute precise numbers from your traces.
[14:02] Priya: One quick question — any blackout windows for rolling updates? we need canary controls.
[14:08] Alex: Redwood rollouts support canary/A-B and automatic fallback. we'll document runbook for safe rollouts.
[14:20] Carlos: Ok great. procurement ramp — if Dedicated looks good, what's the lead time to get GPU capacity reserved?
[14:27] Alex: Typical lead time is 2-6 weeks depending on region and model. we'll try to align with your timeline.
[14:38] Priya: Good — that's acceptable.
[14:42] Samir: any final questions?
[14:45] Ben: Please include an outline of the security posture and how we can get evidence for SOC2.
[14:50] Alex: will do.
[15:00] Alex: ok we'll follow up with the template, docs, and scheduling. thanks everyone.
[15:05] Priya: Thanks all.

End transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: Speaker labels mostly accurate but some words like "KV cache" were auto-transcribed as "K V cash" in some segments; small disfluencies present.
